title: EXAMPLE and SAMPLE as the whole value under credential-named keys
summary: Single-line assignments whose whole value is the English word EXAMPLE or SAMPLE (or a word run built on it, such as EXAMPLE_API_KEY) under credential-named keys: password=EXAMPLE, access_token=SAMPLE, api_key=EXAMPLE_API_KEY, secret: SAMPLE. The values are not a provider's published example and not in any placeholder vocabulary this repository records.
rationale: Two readings are defensible. The word is a documentation placeholder, so reporting it is noise; or it is a literal someone may really use as a password, and a policy that exempts every EXAMPLE or SAMPLE becomes an allowlist for weak real values (an exemption written as a word, not as an exact published literal). The repository's neighbouring records point both ways: placeholder-vocabulary-values treats recognised placeholder spellings as not flagged, placeholder-vocabulary-near-misses and aws-example-keys-one-character-off keep values just outside the vocabulary flagged. Nothing recorded settles whether the bare words EXAMPLE and SAMPLE are inside the vocabulary. They are kept apart from the benign controls so that neither a must-not-flag nor a must-flag count absorbs them.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Settled: the values are not a provider-published literal and carry no provider-documented class. Not settled: whether a bare EXAMPLE or SAMPLE word under a credential-named key is a placeholder (not flagged) or a literal (flagged). Searched: the provider pages already recorded in this repository (AWS IAM access keys, Stripe API keys, Supabase key types); none shows a password or token assignment whose whole value is EXAMPLE or SAMPLE, and no standard defines one. Missing: a maintainer project-policy decision (question, options, chosen outcome, named reviewer, dissent, reversing evidence) or a provider statement. Whether the product masks, redacts or blocks such a value is redact-secret's action policy and is not stated here; credential-eval and redact-secret-benchmarks own execution and qualification. A scanner's behaviour on these inputs is an observation and is not evidence.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
